messages.subject: function if_else's condition
parts:
A problem in 
src/models/bugs_examples/vol1/bones example, which
is close to be working now:

Since we could not handle NA in the R dump data file, 
NA's are changed to -1 (other data are all positive).  Then 
I am using if_else to avoid the missing data. 

Then I am using

lp__ <- lp__ + if_else(data[i] + 1, log(...), zero);  // data[i] = -1 indicates that it is missing


But I seems that when data[i] = -1 src/models/bugs_examples/vol1/bones example, 
log(...) is evaluated instead of return zero. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] function if_else's condition
parts:
A better way to deal with missing data is to
split the data matrix into two:

data_obs[...]
data_miss[...]

and then loop over them separately. You can
then sample the missing data. But if it's discrete,
you'll have to marginalize them out instead.

The definition of if_else is very simple and it's
hard to see where it could go wrong:

template <typename B, typename T>
T if_else(B c, T y_true, T y_false) {
return c ? y_true : y_false;
}

So if_else(c,y_true,y_false) should evaluate
to y_true if c != 0 and to y_false if c == 0.
So if data[i] == -1, then data[i] + 1 should be
0. I'm pretty sure the floating point shouldn't
be going wrong.

The only thing I could think to do here is
instrument if_else and have it print out c
(then remove the instrumentation!).

- Bob
